0.text: 1. Emyiˊrɪk (“in the extending [of the days]”). Loosely speaking, it corresponds to the first month

2.text: 2. Ureˊtvik (“in the lengthening”). This corresponds to the second month.

3.text: 3. Niwleˊwkɪ (“during [the days] growing long”). It lasts about six weeks, until the reindeer-dams

5.text: 4. Am-g̣roˊkĭ (“in the calving [time]”). This corresponds more or less to our term “spring.”
5.corrected: g̣ = g + U+0323 (dot below). My first reading dropped the dot; supplied by editor and confirmed at 5x against the same mark on line 13's G̣. A missed diacritic, recorded as an error against this proposal rather than silently amended.
5.resolved: kĭ = i + U+0306 (breve). ɪ never receives a breve, per editor.
5.note: Not resolvable from the raster at any magnification, and worth knowing why: i loses its dot under an above-diacritic, so printed ĭ is a dotless i with a breve — the same letterform a small-cap ɪ with a breve would present. The mark is a breve (rounded cup), not a caron (wedge), confirmed at 3x. Only the system constraint separates the two candidates. First i+breve in the surviving corpus; the sole existing breve is one u+breve.

18.text: forms; and the people are eloquent in their own way, but they do not like

19.text: to be bored with questions. The Reindeer men, who are in their houses

20.text: practically only when eating or sleeping, and keep in motion all the time,

21.text: were with difficulty persuaded to spend a few hours with me in the tent,

22.text: giving explanations or dictating texts. Even the old men would say, “Bad

23.text: thing, dotage,” and would prefer to stay outside. Most of them, moreover,

24.text: were quite unable to dictate. Even their curiosity is not lasting. When I

25.text: came to a new camp, the inhabitants would pay close attention to my doings

26.text: for a few hours; then they would gradually drop off, and finally would be

27.text: interested only in barter. There were certainly exceptions, as Aiñanwaˊt, whom

28.text: I have mentioned, and a few others. In the Maritime villages, where the

29.text: inner rooms are much larger, and furnished with steadily burning lamps, the

30.text: old people are more used to sitting indoors, and accordingly are more tractable

31.text: and more useful for scientific investigation.
